page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2458 GB SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a PassMark memory score in the top 10% (2978.82) and a cached small-block read memory bandwidth of 4154.72 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance is also in the top 25%, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 86377.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17837.0. However, large-block uncached memory bandwidth is average, with read speeds at 124.14 GB/sec and write speeds at 62.31 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive database workloads, as evidenced by a PassMark database operations score of 24967.46 and Redis SET operations reaching 63.59 million operations per second. While small LLM inference tasks perform well, text generation on large 70B models is a notable bottleneck, yielding a weak performance of 2.67 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. This server is best utilized for relational databases, in-memory caching, and data analytics rather than large-scale AI model generation.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 32-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs, 512.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 2458 GB local SSD. Benchmark results show top-tier memory performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 4154.72 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU capabilities are strong, though uncached large-block memory transfers and large-scale LLM text generation represent performance tradeoffs. With high memory density and strong database benchmark results, including 63.59 million Redis SET operations per second, this instance is configured for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, and in-memory caching workloads.
